displayContract.byline: Assessments made by 5.6 Sol. — Rubric: Slugfester Reassessment Rubric v2.

thesis.text: The AI steelman is that Christian theism is warranted by the joint explanatory force of cosmic origin, objective normativity, and resurrection evidence, provided its account of suffering supplies a principled asymmetry rather than mere possibility.

novelty.explanation: It repairs the live cumulative route by making the unresolved asymmetry requirement an explicit condition of success.

premises.text: If the finite temporal order began and lacks an internal sufficient cause, an agent-causal explanation is a serious candidate because a timeless sufficient mechanical condition would not readily explain a temporally finite effect.

novelty.explanation: It extends the personal-cause inference with an explicit contrast between agent causation and an eternally sufficient mechanical condition.

premises.text: Irreducibly authoritative moral duties fit better with a necessarily good personal source than with either an evil creator or purely descriptive natural facts, although this comparison must engage non-theistic moral realism directly.

novelty.explanation: It repairs the exclusive grounding claim by stating it comparatively and acknowledging the strongest non-theistic rival.

premises.text: The resurrection evidence has weight only insofar as the particular conjunction of early proclamation, claimed appearances, empty-tomb tradition, and contextual expectations is substantially less likely under combined ordinary explanations than under divine action.

novelty.explanation: It repairs the historical inference by incorporating the comparative likelihood and base-rate test raised against it.

premises.text: Skeptical limits concerning providential consequences should reduce confidence rather than erase evidence, while independent reasons for necessary goodness may make suffering under a good creator less symmetric with goodness under an essentially evil creator.

novelty.explanation: It repairs the overstrong skeptical-theist claim and identifies the independent moral asymmetry the live reply lacked.

conclusion.text: Therefore, Christian theism may be the best cumulative explanation if its moral foundation, historical likelihood comparison, and principled response to suffering survive their strongest alternatives; the premises support comparative warrant, not certainty.

novelty.explanation: It repairs the cumulative conclusion by limiting it to comparative warrant conditional on the disputed bridges.

newArguments.title: Modal moral asymmetry
newArguments.text: A necessarily perfect source and an essentially malicious creator need not be evidential mirror images. Perfect goodness can coherently permit limited harms for goods involving free agency, stable causation, rescue, or relationship, whereas perfect malice would have reason to prevent every uncompensated good unless it served greater harm. If independent moral reasoning favors necessary goodness, the two hypotheses generate different constraints on permission and intention. This does not dissolve suffering, but it turns the challenge into a comparative question about which mixed world is more plausible under each constrained character.

novelty.explanation: This introduces a new modal comparison between the permission structures of necessary goodness and essential malice.

newArguments.title: Cross-domain explanatory coherence
newArguments.text: A cumulative case gains force when its components constrain one another rather than merely adding isolated probabilities. A personal origin hypothesis identifies the kind of cause available; a necessary moral nature narrows that cause's character; and a historically situated act of revelation predicts that such a cause might disclose purposes through public events. The resurrection claim should therefore be evaluated under both generic historical baselines and the prior supplied by the other arguments. This dependence prevents simple score-adding, but it can yield coherence if each component independently clears a modest evidential threshold.

novelty.explanation: This introduces a new constraint-based model of cumulative support rather than restating any single live argument.

thesis.text: The AI steelman is that observed suffering substantially lowers the probability of the perfectly good Christian God because the affirmative arguments do not establish a moral or historical asymmetry strong enough to defeat the evil-creator comparison.

novelty.explanation: It extends the negative route by expressing its central challenge as a unified comparative-probability thesis.

premises.text: The evidential datum is not merely that suffering exists, but that it is immense, ancient, unevenly distributed, often unrelated to responsible choice, and frequently destructive without an observable compensating benefit.

novelty.explanation: It extends the suffering argument by specifying pattern-sensitive evidence beyond the bare existence of pain.

premises.text: A defense based only on possible freedom, stable laws, character formation, compensation, or unknown purposes has little discriminatory force when a structurally parallel story can reconcile abundant goodness with an evil creator.

novelty.explanation: It extends the mirroring argument by stating the precise requirement of discriminatory rather than merely possibility-making force.

premises.text: Even a successful argument for a transcendent personal cause would remain neutral regarding perfect goodness, so it cannot offset suffering until a separate argument reliably identifies the cause's moral character.

novelty.explanation: It extends the scope objection by connecting moral neutrality directly to the cumulative evidential balance.

premises.text: Objective morality, if it exists, does not by itself select theism unless divine grounding outperforms non-theistic realism and avoids making goodness depend circularly on the nature of the deity whose goodness is disputed.

novelty.explanation: It repairs the live critique by supplying a substantive rival-grounding burden instead of relying chiefly on cited disagreement.

premises.text: Resurrection reports warrant divine intervention only if their detailed evidential profile is markedly less expected under ordinary testimonial, legendary, psychological, and social mechanisms considered jointly than under resurrection.

novelty.explanation: It extends the base-rate objection by identifying the combined ordinary mechanisms requiring explicit likelihood comparison.

conclusion.text: Therefore, absent a demonstrated asymmetry in moral grounding, providential prediction, or resurrection likelihood, the cumulative evidence warrants withholding belief in the perfectly good Christian God and treating suffering as substantial contrary evidence.

novelty.explanation: It extends the live conclusion while proportionately recommending withholding belief rather than claiming deductive disproof.

newArguments.title: Predictive specificity test
newArguments.text: Unknown-purpose defenses become evidentially costly when they protect a hypothesis from every possible observation. A good-God account should specify, at least approximately, why some distributions of suffering are more expected than others: for example, why nonhuman suffering predates human agency, why harms fall so unevenly, or why many victims receive no visible developmental benefit. Without risky expectations, providential explanations accommodate the data after the fact but do not predict them. The evil-creator mirror exposes this weakness because equally flexible unknown goods can immunize the opposite moral hypothesis against abundant goodness.

novelty.explanation: This introduces a new predictive-specificity criterion for comparing flexible providential explanations.

newArguments.title: Dependence-adjusted resurrection evidence
newArguments.text: Several resurrection data points may not provide independent support if they descend from overlapping traditions, shared communities, or later interpretation of the same experiences. A rigorous comparison should model those dependencies before multiplying the force of the empty tomb, appearances, and transformed belief. It should also compare resurrection with combinations of ordinary causes rather than demand one natural explanation reproduce every detail. This approach grants that the reports can remain historically striking while preventing correlated testimony from being counted repeatedly as though each item independently overcame the low baseline probability of bodily resurrection.

novelty.explanation: This introduces a new dependence-adjustment argument for evaluating the combined historical evidence.
